prompt: What natural plant source did aspirin originally come from?
Explain how vaccination protects a person against a disease, and why it means they respond faster if they meet the real pathogen later.
indicativeContent: A vaccine contains a small, safe amount of a dead or inactive pathogen, or parts of it
This triggers the immune system to produce antibodies specific to that pathogen's antigens, without causing the disease
Memory cells are produced as part of this response
If the real pathogen is met later, memory cells recognise it immediately and antibodies are produced much faster
This faster response usually destroys the pathogen before symptoms of the disease develop
A full-marks answer explains both halves: how the vaccine works, and why the later response is faster
